resource.name: Education Chicago
resource.description: This dataset contains school-level performance metrics used to produce the 2011-2012 CPS School Report Cards. It includes survey-based indicators from the 5 Essentials (such as safety, family involvement, environment, instruction, leadership, and teacher collaboration), parent engagement measures, attendance and misconduct rates, IEP compliance, literacy and math benchmarks across grade levels, student growth metrics, standardized test performance (ISAT, EXPLORE, PLAN, ACT), algebra participation and passing rates, college readiness and eligibility measures, graduation and college enrollment rates, Freshman On-Track rate, and related school identifiers. NDA indicates 'No Data Available.'

Student Perception/Safety category from 5 Essentials survey
The score from the 5 Essentials survey for the Safety category, which reflects students' perceptions of their school's safety.
An index representing the level of parental involvement based on various engagement metrics such as PTA meetings, volunteer hours, and home visits.
The average daily attendance rate of students, indicating the regularity with which students attend classes.
The percentage of students who have been disciplined, indicating the level of behavioral issues within the school.
The percentage of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) that are compliant with CPS guidelines, indicating the quality of special education services.
The percentage of students meeting or exceeding literacy benchmarks, indicating the overall reading proficiency of the student body.
The percentage of students meeting or exceeding math benchmarks, indicating the overall math proficiency of the student body.
An index representing the average growth in student achievement over time, indicating the effectiveness of instructional practices.
An index representing the overall performance of students on standardized tests like ISAT, EXPLORE, PLAN, and ACT, indicating academic achievement.
The percentage of students participating in Algebra courses, indicating the extent to which the school offers advanced coursework.
The percentage of students who pass Algebra courses, indicating the success rate of the school's curriculum and teaching methods.
An index representing the proportion of students who are college-ready based on various criteria such as GPA, test scores, and course completion.
The percentage of students who graduate within four years, indicating the school's ability to retain and educate students through to graduation.
The percentage of graduates who enroll in college immediately after high school, indicating the school's success in preparing students for post-secondary education.
